concepts.title: Class Mark of a Class Interval
concepts.definition: The central value that represents a grouped class interval, calculated by taking the average of its boundary limits.
concepts.key_idea: Midpoint of lower and upper limits serves as the representative value for a class interval.
question_patterns: find the class mark for class interval lower_limit to upper_limit
calculate the midpoint of a class given lower limit lower_limit and upper limit upper_limit
determine the central value of interval lower_limit dash upper_limit
what is the class mark corresponding to class lower_limit to upper_limit
compute the average of class limits lower_limit and upper_limit

solution_steps.action: add lower and upper class limits

solution_steps.explain: divide the sum of limits by 2 to find the class mark

concepts.title: Mean of Grouped Data by Direct Method
concepts.definition: The arithmetic average obtained by summing the products of class frequencies and class marks, then dividing by total frequency.
concepts.key_idea: Divide the aggregate value of all observations by the total count.
question_patterns: find the mean using direct method when sum_fx is aggregate product and sum_f is total frequency
calculate the mean given total weighted score sum_fx and total frequency sum_f
compute the average using direct approach with sum_fx and sum_f
what is the mean mark when sum_fx and sum_f are known
determine mean from sum of fx sum_fx and total sum of frequencies sum_f

solution_steps.explain: divide total sum of products sum_fx by sum of frequencies sum_f

concepts.title: Mean by Assumed Mean Method
concepts.definition: A simplified technique for mean calculation where deviations from an assumed central value are averaged and added back to that central value.
concepts.key_idea: Adjust an assumed central mark by adding the average deviation.
question_patterns: find the mean using assumed mean method with assumed mean a, sum of deviations sum_fd, and sum_f
calculate the mean when assumed mean is a, sum_fd is total deviation product, and total frequency is sum_f

solution_steps.explain: divide sum_fd by total frequency sum_f

solution_steps.action: add assumed mean to average deviation
solution_steps.explain: add assumed mean a to mean_d to get final mean

concepts.title: Mean by Step-Deviation Method
concepts.definition: A computational shortcut for mean where deviations are divided by class size before calculating total product sum.
concepts.key_idea: Scale down deviations by class width to simplify multiplication, then scale back up.
question_patterns: find the mean by step deviation method given assumed mean a, class size h, sum_fu, and sum_f

solution_steps.explain: multiply mean_u by class width h
add assumed mean a to scaled deviation

concepts.title: Mode of Grouped Data
concepts.definition: The central value having highest frequency in a grouped distribution, calculated using lower limit, modal frequency, adjacent frequencies, and class width.
concepts.key_idea: Interpolate within the highest-frequency class interval using adjacent class frequencies.
question_patterns: find the mode of grouped data with lower limit l, class size h, modal frequency f1, preceding frequency f0, and succeeding frequency f2

multiply (num / den) by class size h

concepts.title: Median of Grouped Data
concepts.definition: The value that divides a grouped distribution into two equal halves, computed using median class lower limit, cumulative frequency, frequency, and class width.
concepts.key_idea: Locate the 50th percentile mark within the median class interval.

concepts.title: Empirical Relationship Between Central Tendencies
concepts.definition: An empirical rule connecting mode, median, and mean in moderately skewed distributions.
concepts.key_idea: Three times median equals mode plus twice mean.
question_patterns: find the mode using empirical formula when median and mean are given
